description: Grade 5 example: write an interval under a key signature (E minor, bass clef).

provenance.authoredBy: Music Theory Path curriculum team (Brief 10 addendum)

item.prompt: The key signature of E minor is shown. Write the note a major 3rd up from this note, adding an accidental only if the key signature does not already give it.

music.textAlternative: One minim, B2, under the key signature of E minor.

hints: Find the letter name first, then decide what the interval needs on that letter.
Then compare with the key signature: write a sign only for the difference.

feedback.correct: Correct. B up a major 3rd is D♯. E minor's signature has only F♯, so the D♯ needs its own sharp sign (it is the raised 7th).

mistakes.redundant-or-missing-accidental: B up a major 3rd is D♯. E minor's signature has only F♯, so the D♯ needs its own sharp sign (it is the raised 7th).
mistakes.accidental-not-applied: Check what the key signature already gives that letter before adding a sign. B up a major 3rd is D♯. E minor's signature has only F♯, so the D♯ needs its own sharp sign (it is the raised 7th).
mistakes.enharmonic-spelling: That sounds the same but uses the wrong letter name. An interval's number fixes the letter: count the letter names from the starting note.

feedback.fallback: B up a major 3rd is D♯. E minor's signature has only F♯, so the D♯ needs its own sharp sign (it is the raised 7th).
